analysis.title: USA: Consumer Confidence Well Above Expectations; New Home Sales Decline Less Than Expected
key_insights: The Conference Board consumer confidence index rose 7.5pt to 91.7 in October from an upwardly revised September reading of 84.2, well above the 81.0 GS and median forecasts. It is now in line with levels from the beginning of the year.
Both components rose from upwardly revised September levels. The present situation index gained 8.6pt to 120.4 and the expectations index gained 6.9pt to 72.6.

The labor differential (share saying jobs are plentiful minus share saying jobs are hard to get) rose 2.4pp to 5.3%, reversing its large decline last month. Jobs plentiful rose 2.4pp to 26.7% and jobs hard to get was flat at 21.4%.
Median 12-month ahead inflation expectations fell 0.4pp to 4.7% but remain 0.2pp above the February level, just before the start of the war.

In write-in responses, references to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices continued to rise. Comments about war/conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. The cutoff date for preliminary results was October 21.

New single-family home sales fell 0.6% to a 676k SAAR in September, a smaller decline than the GS forecast of -4.8% (651k) and the median forecast of -4.5% (651k). August was revised down 4k to 680k SAAR.

September new home sales fell in the South (-6.6%) and Midwest (-7.3%), partly retracing the largest one-month percent increase in the series' history in August. Sales rose in the Northeast (+28.0%) and West (+21.4%).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Well above the 81.0 GS and median forecasts and the revised prior of 84.2. Confidence is back to levels from the start of the year.
